stem.en: Between the Lower and Middle Palaeolithic, the toolkit changed. Sort each item into the period it characterises.

image.alt: Two plates of stone tools side by side: on the left, large pear-shaped handaxes, broad cleavers and heavy choppers; on the right, much smaller thin flake tools - steep scrapers, pointed borers and slim points.

text.en: Tool made on a thin flake

explanation.en: The Lower Palaeolithic is the age of big tools: handaxes, cleavers and choppers. The Middle Palaeolithic toolkit is made on thin flakes: borers for making holes, and points small enough to tip a projectile. Scrapers appear in both periods, so they are not in this sort. Rock types and bone-splitting are left out for the same reason.

hints.en: Ask first: is this a large tool worked from the whole stone, or a small tool worked on a thin flake?
